original_question: For a simple connected unsigned graph Γ, determine the signature or signatures σ̄ that minimize spectral radius among all signatures on Γ, that is, satisfy ρ(Γ, σ̄) <= ρ(Γ, σ) for every signature σ of Γ.
target_in_paper: Section 3.5, Problem 3.18 (Signature minimizing the spectral radius). The draft is targeting this exact open problem, rather than the later sufficient-bound variant Problem 3.26 or the special-family question raised after Proposition 3.27. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official formulation almost verbatim: it fixes a simple connected unsigned graph, quantifies over all signatures on that fixed underlying graph, and asks for the signature(s) attaining the minimum spectral radius through the condition ρ(Γ,σ̄)≤ρ(Γ,σ) for every signature σ. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
missing_details: Make explicit that a signature is a map σ:E(Γ)→{+1,−1}. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

Define ρ(Γ,σ) as the spectral radius of the real signed adjacency matrix Aσ, where (Aσ)uv=σ(uv) when uv is an edge of Γ and 0 otherwise. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

If the question is to be fully stand-alone, note that for signed graphs the spectral radius need not equal the largest eigenvalue, so ρ must be understood as max{|λ|: λ∈spec(Aσ)} rather than λ1(Aσ). ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

Clarify that the minimization is over all edge-signings of the fixed underlying graph Γ, not over different graphs. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

If one wants a classification rather than a raw list, it is natural to identify minimizers up to switching equivalence, because switching-equivalent signings are similar/cospectral and therefore have the same spectral radius; however, the official problem itself is phrased directly in terms of signatures. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
refined_question: Let Γ be a simple connected unsigned graph with edge set E(Γ). For each signature σ:E(Γ)→{+1,−1}, let Aσ be the real signed adjacency matrix defined by (Aσ)uv=σ(uv) if uv∈E(Γ) and (Aσ)uv=0 otherwise, and let ρ(Γ,σ)=ρ(Aσ)=max{|λ|: λ is an eigenvalue of Aσ}. Determine all signatures σ̄:E(Γ)→{+1,−1} such that ρ(Γ,σ̄)=min_{σ:E(Γ)→{+1,−1}} ρ(Γ,σ), equivalently, such that ρ(Γ,σ̄)≤ρ(Γ,σ) for every signature σ of Γ. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, determine the switching-equivalence class(es) of signatures on Γ that minimize the spectral radius, since switching-equivalent signings have similar signed adjacency matrices and hence the same spectrum and spectral radius. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
justification: The paper first defines signatures, signed adjacency matrices, and spectral radius in the introduction, then proves in Theorem 2.5 that no signing can have larger spectral radius than the all-positive signing, and in Section 3.5 immediately asks for the opposite extremal problem: which signature minimizes the spectral radius on a fixed simple connected unsigned graph. That is exactly your draft. The later discussion in the same subsection gives motivation from expander/Ramanujan signings and then introduces a different bound-seeking question (Problem 3.26) plus a special-family follow-up after Proposition 3.27, so the sharpest paper-faithful rewrite is simply a fully self-contained version of Problem 3.18 itself. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

citations.label: adjacency matrix, spectral radius, and switching equivalence/cospectrality
